prompt_text: I need a dental implant in Columbus. Which specific dental practices should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Columbus Ohio for a dental implant?
answer_verbatim:
I can do that — first a quick question so I give you useful recommendations: which “Columbus” do you mean (Columbus, OH? Columbus, GA? another city)? Also tell me any preferences: do you have a dentist you want to keep for the crown/restoration, do you have dental insurance, do you need sedation, and is cost or speed the top priority?

If you want me to look up specific practices where you live, say the city/ZIP and I’ll pull a short list of well-rated oral surgeons / periodontists / implant centers to call, with phone/address and why each is a good choice.

Meanwhile, here are immediate, practical suggestions so you know what to look for when I compile options:

Which types of practices to call (and why)
- Board-certified oral & maxillofacial surgeons — best for complex surgery, bone grafting, sedation/general anesthesia, and patients with medical issues.
- Periodontists (gum specialists) — many focus on implants and bone grafting and often do very good esthetic implant work.
- Prosthodontists — experts in the crown/bridge part of the implant (important for complex restorations, full-arch work, or cosmetic outcomes).
- Dedicated implant centers (multi-specialty clinics) — convenient if they handle surgery and restoration in-house, with digital planning, CBCT imaging, and a lab relationship.

What to ask when you call (use these exact questions)
1. Do you place dental implants in-house or refer out? Who will restore the implant (your office or my general dentist)?
2. Are you a board-certified oral surgeon/periodontist/prosthodontist? How many implants do you place per year?
3. Do you use CBCT (3D) imaging and guided implant planning? Is that included in the consult?
4. Which implant systems/brands do you use? (Nobel, Straumann, Zimmer, etc. — established brands are preferable.)
5. Do you provide bone grafting/sinus lifts if needed? What’s the additional cost?
6. What sedation/anesthesia options are available and who administers them?
7. What is the estimated timeline from extraction to finished crown (or for a full-arch solution)?
8. What are the out-of-pocket costs (consult, imaging, surgery, implant, abutment, crown)? Do you offer payment plans/financing?
9. What is your implant success rate and warranty/guarantee policy if an implant fails?
10. Do you accept my insurance? Do you file claims?

What to bring to the consultation
- Any recent dental X-rays or CT scans (or authorize them to take a CBCT there).
- A list of current medications, medical history, and tobacco use.
- Your general dentist’s name/records (if you want them to coordinate).

Ballpark timing and cost (very general)
- Single implant + abutment + crown: commonly $2,000–$5,000+ depending on region, grafting, and implant brand.
- Full-arch options (All-on-4 / fixed bridges): typically much more ($15k–$40k+ per arch).
- If bone grafting or sinus lift needed, expect additional procedures and months of healing.

If you want, I’ll now look up 5–7 specific, well-reviewed practices in Columbus (with phone/address and a short reason to call each). Tell me which Columbus or give a ZIP, and whether you prefer specialists (oral surgeon or periodontist), or to prioritize price, speed, or highest expertise.
